rules.title: Scoring
rules.summary: A match is the best of three games. Each rally won scores one point. A game is played to 21, with a two-point lead required at 20-all and a maximum of 30. The side winning a game serves first in the next game.
rules.example: 21–20 does not end the game; 30–29 does.

rules.title: Changing ends
rules.summary: Players change ends after the first game, after the second game if there is a third, and when a side first reaches 11 points in the third game. If they forget, correct this when the shuttle is out of play and keep the existing score.
rules.example: At 11–8 in the third game, the players change ends.

rules.title: Service and receiving positions
rules.summary: Server and receiver stand within diagonally opposite service courts without touching boundary lines. Some part of both feet must remain in stationary contact with the court from the start until the service is delivered.
rules.example: A served shuttle may land on the applicable line, but a server’s foot touching a service-court line is a fault.

rules.title: Service action
rules.summary: Do not unduly delay. Release the shuttle without adding spin; hit its base first while the whole shuttle is below 1.15 m at racket contact. Continue the racket’s forward movement and do not miss the shuttle. The shuttle must travel upward over the net toward the diagonal receiving court. The receiver must be ready; an attempted return shows readiness. Partners must not obscure the server or receiver.
rules.example: Serving below the height limit does not excuse adding spin when releasing the shuttle.

rules.title: Singles service
rules.summary: At an even server score, serve from the right service court; at an odd score, serve from the left. If the server wins the rally, they serve again from the other court. If the receiver wins, they score and become the server.
rules.example: A server with seven points stands in the left service court; if they win, they serve from the right at eight points.

rules.title: Doubles service and receiving order
rules.summary: The serving side uses its right service court at an even score and its left at an odd score; the receiver stands diagonally opposite. Players change service courts only when their side wins a point while serving. After the return of service, either partner may hit the shuttle when it is their side’s turn.
rules.example: If A1 serves and B1 initially receives, successive new servers after service changes are A1 → B2 → A2 → B1 → A1. The current server continues if their side wins a rally.

rules.title: Service-court and order errors
rules.summary: Correct service-court or serving/receiving order errors when the shuttle is out of play. Keep points already scored.
rules.example: Finding that the wrong player received after a rally does not erase earlier points.

rules.title: In and out
rules.summary: A shuttle landing on an applicable boundary line is in. The doubles long service line is closer to the net than the back boundary used during a rally.
rules.example: A shuttle landing between the doubles long service line and the back boundary is out on doubles service but may be in during a rally.

rules.title: Common faults
rules.summary: Faults include illegal service; a shuttle landing out or touching a person or ceiling; catching and slinging it; successive hits by both partners; touching the net while the shuttle is in play; obstruction; or deliberate distraction.
rules.example: A racket following through over the net after contact on the striker’s side is not automatically a fault, provided it does not obstruct the opponent. One stroke touching both the frame and strings is not automatically a double hit.

rules.title: Lets
rules.summary: A let may be called when the receiver is not ready, both sides fault during service, or another Law 14 condition applies. The rally does not count and the previous server serves again.
rules.example: After a return of service, a shuttle caught on the net is a let. If it is caught on the net during service, Law 13.2 makes it a fault instead.

rules.title: Shuttle not in play
rules.summary: A shuttle is not in play after it hits the court, a fault or let occurs, or it hits the net or post and starts falling toward the striker’s court.
rules.example: Do not assume that every shuttle contact with the net ends the rally.
